reviews.title: Brilliant; but insultingly limited as a “free” app. Only “Premium” upgrade available, $30/mo
reviews.text:
tl;dr, this needs a $10/mo paid tier. 

I’m sure this app is brilliant - if you pay $30/mo. The free experience gets you one “warm up” (recycled review content) and one new lesson (5-10min) per day. 

Every day, you get to watch one unskippable video ad for Premium (because you obviously forgot about it in the last 24hrs), 3 FOMO notifications, and a nag screen that again makes you confirm that you choose to suck instead of paying a couple hundred bucks a year. 

The mood while learning is warm and cozy, but claiming that they give you 2 keys each day, nagging you to not break your streak, and then forcing you to burn half of your daily “learning” allowance on content you just did yesterday… feels insulting and disingenuous. 

I happily pay $10-15 per app every month for several apps that respect my wallet and intelligence. I’ve got a week or two streak going here, but every time I leave this app feeling mildly insulted - not inspired or “wanting more”.

Free is almost useless, and $30/mo feels way out of line for the level of content I’m seeing as a free user. I mean, $30/mo will get you access to multiple massive libraries of streaming educational content and masterclass style courses… this app is very nicely designed, but the value prop feels waaaaaay off.

reviews.title: My jaw is on the floor
reviews.text: I’ve been a teacher for most of my professional life and I’m astonished at how perfectly constructed these courses are. The structure is everything— the way material is introduced incrementally and constantly being reviewed and revisited in subtle ways makes the learning intuitive. I decided to try the course on circuits because the teacher in me was curious how this app would structure the lessons and I was blown away by how perfectly rock solid the layering of learning is. Despite having studied circuits in college as part of my mechanical engineering degree, I find myself intuiting the answers to the questions in this course in a way I never had mental access to before. It’s like this course is restructuring my understanding from the atomic level up so that the correct answers become inevitable. All the professors with PhDs that I payed thousands to learn from have got nothing compared to this!

I will say, while doing the variable courses, the blocks and shapes were confusing at first. Because they are so simple, I couldn’t tell what operation it wanted me to do, as the blocks represent numbers and variables. The blocks don’t really indicate what I was really meant to do in other words. It also placed me on lessons I already knew much about, and it kinda annoys me how I have to review old material for ages just to learn new things. I think maybe adding a test system to skip ahead or perhaps improving the beginning “trial” to be more thorough and accurate would solve this issue. Maybe taking inspo from the IXL arena could be very beneficial to new users. Other than that, I love this app,and hope to use this often in the future!

reviews.title: Accessibility Barrier: Misleading Visual Puzzle Rules
reviews.text: The visual fraction puzzles are an accessibility nightmare for neurodivergent learners. Asking someone to "Color 1/2 of the shape" on a grid composed of unequal block sizes without explicit instructions forces users to guess whether to count boxes or calculate area. Neurodivergent people who process visual layout literally are left struggling. You need to provide proper instructions or visual grid overlays to fix this. Please respond with how your team plans to address this accessibility barrier.
